# The Bet · FinWise

> Module 1 · Ignite a PLG Motion. The growth hypothesis and where you're betting, plus the growth-loop visualization.

## Growth hypothesis

FinWise's biggest growth problem is FinWise's biggest growth problem is that 98.0% of trial users never convert to paid; trial → paid sits near 2% in every month., because because (my assumption, not shown in the data) trial users work alone, so nothing shared ties them to the product and they have no work to pay to keep..

_Working notes: I think FinWise's biggest problem is that trial users don't reach the product's core value before the trial ends, so very few convert to paid. Evidence: I think this because:
1. Only 2% of trial users convert to paid, which is the steepest drop in the funnel.
2. Adding more acquisition spend no longer drives meaningful growth, so more sign-ups aren't turning into customers.
3. FinWise runs a reverse trial, which only works if users experience the value they stand to lose. Against the data: The data confirmed where the leak is (trial → paid, 98.0% of trials don't convert) but challenged my explanation. Import Data % ranged from 30.5% to 45.4% while trial → paid stayed near 2%, with a correlation of -0.05 across the 13 months. Monthly totals can't show what individual trial users do, so I now treat "users don't reach core value" as unproven and would need user-level trial data to test it._

_____

## The bet

the highest-leverage experiment I'd run first is an A/B test that prompts trial users to invite their accountant or bookkeeper right after they build their first report, measured on trial → paid (primary) and invites sent per trial user (secondary).

**Not doing:** I'm not going after paid acquisition or retention because focusing there would pull effort from the bet above: the scenario says extra acquisition spend no longer drives growth, and retention can wait until the bet shows whether more trials convert.

_____

## Growth loop

**Loop type:** Collaboration, I would experiment with a Collaboration loop because small-business finance work is shared with accountants, bookkeepers and co-owners, so a trial user who invites them creates dependency and a reason to upgrade. The dataset has no invite or sharing data, so this is a bet to test, not something the data shows.
